{{Short description|Theorem in order theory}}
{{More footnotes needed|date=April 2026}}
In mathematics, '''Markowsky's theorem''' states: every [[chain-complete]] [[poset]] is a [[Directed complete partial order|dcpo]] where
*a poset is ''chain-complete'' if each chain in it has a least upper bound.
*a poset is a ''dcpo'' if each directed set in it has a least upper bound.
Since a dcpo is chain-complete (as a chain is directed), the converse of the theorem is trivial.

A known proof uses [[Iwamura's lemma]] and [[Ordinal number|ordinal]]s.<ref>{{harvnb|Goubault-Larrecq|2015}}</ref>
